title: Paw Patrol Pre-Writing Worksheets — Character-Driven Stroke Practice

overview.description: 7 landscape-oriented pre-writing stroke worksheets using Paw Patrol characters as motivation. Each page: character on the left, stroke tracing lines in the middle, character(s) on the right as the 'destination.' Narrative framing: 'Help Ryder find his rescue dogs!' The child traces waves, straight lines, vertical lines, zigzags, etc. to 'connect' characters to each other or to bones. Progressive difficulty: solid guide lines → dotted guide lines → dot-to-dot (fade scaffolding).

characterMotivation.description: Paw Patrol characters (Ryder, Marshall, Rubble, Chase, Skye) serve as the START and END points of tracing lines. The child isn't 'practicing strokes' — they're 'helping Ryder find his dogs' or 'getting the dogs to their bones.' The beloved character IS the motivation.
characterMotivation.value: Engagement through familiarity. A reluctant writer will trace a line to get to Chase when they won't trace a line because the teacher said so.

fadingScaffolding.description: Within a single page, guide lines progress from solid (fully supported) → dotted (partially supported) → dot-to-dot (minimal support). The child experiences increasing independence on the same page. Row 1 has solid guides; row 3 has only dots to connect.
fadingScaffolding.value: Gradual release of responsibility within a single activity. The child builds confidence before the scaffolding disappears.

narrativeFraming.description: 'Help Ryder find his rescue dogs!' and 'Get the rescue dogs to their bones!' turn abstract motor practice into a story. The tracing IS the quest.
narrativeFraming.value: Pre-writing practice disguised as play. The child doesn't know they're 'doing school.'

landscapeOrientation.description: Pages are landscape, not portrait. This gives more horizontal room for stroke practice — the child's arm moves across the full width of the page.
landscapeOrientation.value: Ergonomically correct for left-to-right stroke development.

difficulty.complexity: single-skill per page with progressive scaffolding fade
difficulty.scaffolding: very high → medium (fades within each page)

gaps.name: character-themed-tracing
gaps.description: Pre-writing stroke pages where the child's favorite character is at the START and a destination (another character, treat, or goal) is at the END of each tracing line. Narrative framing turns tracing into a quest. Fading scaffolding (solid → dotted → dots) within a single page. Landscape orientation for full arm movement. Homa's version would use original characters (not copyrighted IP) but the PATTERN is what matters.

notes: This drop is interesting because it's the ONLY one from either user that uses licensed/commercial characters (Paw Patrol = Nickelodeon IP). Everything else has been original art or nature-themed. The signal isn't 'use Paw Patrol' — it's 'character-driven motivation works for reluctant pre-writers.' Homa could generate character-themed tracing pages using original Homa characters. The fading scaffolding pattern (solid → dotted → dots within one page) is also new and valuable. Compare to CKLA pre-writing (poem-as-instruction with themed illustrations) — two different approaches to the same skill, both valid.
